title: How could we name a turn and say how big it is?
description: A gate and a window shutter stand open by different amounts, then a book cover and the hands of a clock join them. Each one turns, and some turn more than others, so the video ends on the open question of how to name a turn and say how big it is.
teaching_notes: One idea: a turn can be small or large, and we want a way to name it and measure it. Watch for students who call out a number before the chapter has shown how a turn is measured.

source: Where do bends and turns hide?
video_script.why: Before any new word, the child sees that gates, book covers and clock hands all turn, and wonders how to name and measure a turn.
video_script.substitution: Picture a gate, a book cover and the hands of a clock, and ask how to measure a turn.
video_script.anchor: an old iron gate and a window shutter open by different amounts, with a book cover and the hands of a clock beside them

names.Ruhee: the child who opens the book cover, the book's own character

maths_rules: The gate and the shutter are open by different amounts, one a little and one wide.
The book cover opens a little and then wider.
No angle mark and no number is drawn anywhere.
The open question, how to name a turn and say how big it is, is never answered.
video_script.design: One idea: turns differ in size and we want to name and measure them. The pictures arrive one by one and all stay to the end. Nothing is named or measured.
